enriched_description: Small burrowing decapod crustacean measuring 2-5 cm in carapace width with highly asymmetrical claw morphology in males. Male exhibits one massively enlarged claw (cheliped) comprising up to half of total body weight, while the other claw remains small and functional for feeding. Enlarged claw is smooth, rounded, and brightly colored in red, orange, yellow, or white. Female has two small equal claws. Carapace is squarish to trapezoidal with smooth surface, displaying grey, brown, or greenish coloration with darker mottling. Eyes are stalked and positioned at anterior carapace corners. Four pairs of walking legs are slender with flattened terminal segments adapted for rapid sideways locomotion. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry. Weight ranges 1-10 grams.

Very large edible decapod crustacean with broad spiny carapace measuring 20-28 cm in width and leg span reaching 1.5-1.8 meters. Carapace is rounded to heart-shaped with prominent spines and tubercles covering surface, displaying reddish-brown to purple-brown coloration with lighter mottling. Five pairs of extremely long, robust walking legs covered with sharp spines, particularly on first three pairs. First pair modified into moderately sized claws, smaller relative to body than true crabs. Eyes are stalked and small relative to massive body size. Abdomen is reduced and folded ventrally. Exoskeleton is thick, heavily calcified, and rough-textured due to spination. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry. Weight ranges 4-10 kg, with some specimens exceeding 12 kg.

Large marine decapod crustacean with elongated cylindrical body measuring 30-60 cm in total length. Body is segmented with hard calcified exoskeleton displaying dark bluish-green to brownish-green coloration, sometimes with orange or yellow mottling. Anterior body features large asymmetrical claws: one massive crusher claw with blunt rounded teeth, one smaller cutter claw with sharp inner edges. Both claws are covered with small spines and tubercles. Head-thorax (cephalothorax) is protected by smooth carapace with prominent rostral spines. Five pairs of walking legs extend from thorax, first three bearing small claws. Abdomen (tail) is muscular and segmented with swimmerets (pleopods) on ventral surface. Tail fan (telson and uropods) is broad and paddle-shaped. Eyes are stalked and compound. Antennae are long and whip-like. Weight ranges 0.5-5 kg, with record specimens exceeding 20 kg.

Large marine decapod crustacean measuring 30-50 cm in body length lacking the enlarged claws characteristic of true lobsters. Body is elongated and cylindrical with hard spiny exoskeleton displaying reddish-brown, purple, or greenish-brown coloration with lighter spots and bands. Carapace is heavily armored with prominent forward-pointing spines and tubercles covering entire surface. Antennae are extremely long, thick, and spiny, exceeding body length, serving as primary defensive structures. Five pairs of walking legs are robust with terminal claws. Abdomen (tail) is muscular and segmented with broad tail fan. Eyes are stalked and prominent. Small first antennae (antennules) are short and brush-like. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry. Texture is rough and heavily spined. Weight ranges 1-5 kg.

Small freshwater decapod crustacean measuring 5-15 cm in body length resembling a miniature lobster. Body is elongated and segmented with hard exoskeleton displaying reddish-brown, greenish-brown, or dark brown coloration. Cephalothorax is protected by smooth carapace with cervical groove visible laterally. First pair of appendages modified into prominent claws (chelipeds), typically equal in size and smaller than marine lobster claws, with serrated inner edges. Remaining four pairs are walking legs with small terminal claws. Abdomen (tail) is muscular and segmented with reduced swimmerets. Tail fan is broad and fan-shaped. Eyes are stalked and compound. Two pairs of antennae: first pair short, second pair long and slender. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry. Exoskeleton texture is smooth to slightly granulated. Weight ranges 30-300 grams.

Small decapod crustacean measuring 2-15 cm inhabiting abandoned gastropod shells for protection. Body exhibits asymmetrical soft abdomen coiled to fit spiral shell interior, with reduced calcification on ventral surface. Anterior body (cephalothorax) is hardened with exoskeleton displaying reddish, brown, or orange coloration with darker mottling. First pair of appendages are unequal claws: one larger for blocking shell aperture, one smaller for feeding. Remaining legs are adapted for gripping shell interior and locomotion. Eyes are stalked and prominent. Antennae are long and segmented. When removed from shell, abdomen reveals soft, pale, uncalcified texture with hooked appendages (pleopods) for shell attachment. Shell selection is species-specific, typically matching body size with spiral gastropod shells. Body exhibits modified bilateral symmetry due to abdominal asymmetry.

Small crustacean with dorsoventrally flattened elongated body measuring 0.5-50 cm depending on species. Body is segmented into head (cephalon), thorax (pereon) with seven pairs of similar walking legs (isopod = equal feet), and abdomen (pleon) ending in uropods. Exoskeleton is hard and calcified in aquatic species, softer in terrestrial forms (pillbugs, sowbugs). Coloration ranges from grey, brown, white, to translucent. Body exhibits clear bilateral symmetry with dorsoventrally flattened profile. Terrestrial species can roll into defensive ball (volvation). Aquatic species are streamlined for crawling. Surface texture is smooth to granulated with visible segmental divisions. Antennae are prominent with multiple segments. Eyes are compound and sessile (not stalked). Weight ranges from milligrams to several grams.

Large wading bird measuring 100-115 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 155-165 cm. Plumage is predominantly brilliant white with contrasting glossy black primary and secondary flight feathers visible in flight. Neck and head are white with fine black feathering around eyes. Bill is long, straight, pointed, and bright red, measuring 15-17 cm. Legs and feet are long and bright red, adapted for wading in shallow water. Wings are broad and flat with black coverts creating sharp demarcation from white body. Tail feathers are black with white undertail coverts. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with elongated neck comprising one-quarter of total length. Juveniles display duller plumage with black bill and legs. Weight ranges 2-4 kg. Flight posture features straight neck extension.

Large wading bird measuring 95-100 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 145-155 cm. Plumage exhibits striking dichromatic pattern: glossy black upperparts displaying iridescent green and purple sheen in direct light, contrasting with pure white underparts from breast to undertail coverts. Head and neck are black with fine elongated feathers creating shaggy appearance. Bill is long, straight, pointed, and bright red, measuring 14-16 cm. Legs and feet are long and bright red, adapted for wading. Wings are broad with black flight feathers matching body coloration. Tail feathers are black with green iridescence. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with elongated neck. Juveniles display brownish-black plumage with duller bill and legs. Weight ranges 2-3 kg. Flight posture features straight neck extension.

Medium to large wading bird measuring 70-95 cm in body length with wingspan reaching 120-140 cm. Most distinctive feature is elongated flat bill with spatulate tip resembling a spoon, measuring 12-18 cm, used for tactile feeding in shallow water. Bill color ranges from black to grey with yellow tip depending on species. Plumage is predominantly white in most species, with some displaying pink, yellow, or black accents. Crest of elongated feathers extends from nape during breeding season. Legs are long and dark grey to black, adapted for wading. Neck is long and S-curved. Wings are broad with colored primary feathers visible in flight. Tail is short and rounded. Body exhibits bilateral symmetry with streamlined profile. Weight ranges 0.5-2 kg. Flight posture features neck retraction in S-curve.
